including T and B lymphocytes also inﬁltrate adipose tissue in obesity. The immune cells interact with adipocytes and an inﬂam-
matory environment is created (Hotamisligl et al., 1993; Tilg and Moschen, 2006; Sethi and Hotamisligl, 2021). This most likely
contributes to the insulin resistance that occurs in obesity. For example, TNF-a results in insulin insensitivity, indirectly by stimu-
lating stress hormone production and directly by sustained induction of SOCS-3, which has been shown to decrease insulin-
induced insulin receptor substrate 1 tyrosine phosphorylation and its association with the p85, the regulatory subunit of
phosphatidylinositol-3 kinase, and by negative regulation of PPAR gamma, an important insulin-sensitizing nuclear receptor.
